title: Easter ’67 poster
lede: Ian McLaren’s poster for the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament’s Easter 1967 march: a field of white dots on black that swell into a glowing disc under a plain grotesque headline.
summary: White dots that grow toward the centre of a black sheet, under “Easter ’67” in white sans-serif. Ian McLaren for CND, 1967.

creator.name: Ian McLaren (artist); Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament (issuer)

evidence.note: Downloaded and inspected the V&A photograph of its copy, E.383-2021 (1110 × 1600 px), photographed on a wooden surface, in a scratchpad. No image is stored.

styles.note: Clear graphic-design use of op art: a black and white dot field that swells by steps, with plain sans-serif type in a separate band.

context: The V&A catalogues the poster with the style “Op Art”, gives Ian McLaren as artist and the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament (CND) as issuer, and dates it 1967. [V&A](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O1664114/).
The V&A record has no further description. The event text on the poster lists Easter Saturday at Grosvenor Square, Easter Sunday at Ruislip, and an Easter Monday march to a rally in Trafalgar Square.
observed: The upper third is a solid black band with the CND symbol in a white disc and “Easter ’67” in large white grotesque capitals and lower case.
Four columns of small white sans-serif text give the organiser’s address and the times and places of the events.
The lower two thirds hold a square field of white dots on black. The dots are small at the edges and grow until they merge near the centre, so a bright, soft-edged disc appears.
The dot field seems to bulge toward the viewer. There is no colour.
interpretation: The poster follows the op rules for type and pattern: the text sits on solid black, apart from the field, and the field does the expressive work.
The swelling dot field can be read as a light or a blast, which gives the abstract device a message without adding a figure.
borrow: Scale a regular dot grid so that the dots grow toward a centre and merge into a bright disc.
Keep all text in a separate solid band above the pattern, set in one plain grotesque at two sizes.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The design is probably in copyright, and the V&A photograph is not openly licensed.
